title: Operation Sohan: Army, J&K Police and CRPF Kill Two Suspected JeM Terrorists in Udhampur Encounter
detail: A joint counter-terrorism operation — 'Operation Sohan' — by the Indian Army's White Knight Corps, Jammu & Kashmir Police and CRPF killed two suspected Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorists during the intervening night of September 16-17, 2026 in the Brattal Sohan and Khubban forest areas of Majalta tehsil, Udhampur district, near the Kathua district border. The operation followed confirmed intelligence inputs on terrorist presence in the area; troops launched a cordon-and-search operation despite hostile weather, difficult high-altitude terrain and poor visibility, resulting in a gunfight in which the two terrorists were killed and arms and ammunition recovered. Some outlets identified the slain men as Saddam and Mustafa, both Pakistani nationals, though the White Knight Corps' initial statement said identities were still being ascertained. No security-force casualties were reported. Search and surveillance operations, including sniffer dogs and aerial assets, continued in the area into September 18, alongside a separate, recently disclosed operation in Rajouri targeting a Lashkar-e-Taiba overground-worker network.

media.caption: Security forces operation in Majalta, Udhampur district, during the Operation Sohan encounter, September 2026

confidenceReason: Confirmed by the Army's White Knight Corps statement and reported consistently across multiple Tier-2 Indian outlets (The Week, Greater Kashmir) and a Tier-3 specialist defence outlet; only the slain terrorists' precise identities remain disputed between sources.

title: Pakistan Extends Airspace Ban on Indian Aircraft to October 24
detail: The Pakistan Airports Authority issued a new Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) extending its closure of Pakistani airspace to Indian-registered aircraft — and planes owned, operated or leased by Indian airlines and operators, including military aircraft — from an earlier September 24 expiry to 4:59am on October 24, 2026. The extension took effect at 10:45am on Wednesday, September 17, and covers both of Pakistan's Flight Information Regions, Karachi (OPKR) and Lahore (OPLR). Pakistan and India imposed matching reciprocal airspace restrictions on each other's carriers after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, and both sides have repeatedly rolled the bans forward in roughly month-long increments since; India's own ban on Pakistani aircraft has similarly been extended through successive NOTAMs. Neither government indicated any change in the underlying diplomatic posture accompanying this latest extension.

media.caption: Pakistan extends its airspace ban on Indian aircraft to October 24, 2026

confidenceReason: Confirmed by the published NOTAM and reported consistently, with matching effective and expiry times, across multiple independent Pakistani Tier-2 outlets (Dawn, The Nation, Pakistan Today).
